convoLines.text: "Do you still count the days? I lost track days ago."
"Good. Keep counting. The days need witnesses. ...sorry."
"Still on what day it is."
"Alone's how I stay alive. Don't take it personal."
"Come get air with me. I need to think out loud."
Somkiat shows you where they go to think. "Don't tell the others. Everyone needs one place."
"...Never mind me. What were you going to say?"
"Have you heard what they're calling The Redactor? Naran is pushing 'The Ugly Beast'. Everyone's got a name for it and nobody agrees."
They nod. "Okay."
You show them Wild Onion — where it grows, how to tell it apart. They nod slowly, committing it to memory. "Good to know. Really good to know."
"I have opinions about the name. I am saving them for when they count."
"Anyway — I should get going."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"This was good." They mean it.
"I keep expecting to see them by the fire. Then I remember."
"Come get air with me. I need to think out loud."
"I buried this before the Scattering. Seemed stupid to keep it secret." Naran digs up a wrapped bundle — food, still good. (+1224 kcal to the pantry.)
The easy manner evaporates. What's left is watching you back.
"Fine." Sharp. "You want to hear it? I dug it up. I was starving and your hole was right there. Happy now?"
They shake their head, then nod — both true at once. "Talk to me a bit. That helps more than anything."
"The whole fire was arguing about The Redactor last night — what to even CALL it. 'Old Ugly' got shouted down. What's your vote?"
"Take your time."
"Alone's how I stay alive. Don't take it personal."
"And... scene. Good talk."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"Thanks for... you know. Just listening."
"This was good." They mean it.
"It's stupid. I'm alive, everyone's alive, and I can't stop shaking. Give it time."
"Most days I don't think about it. Today I am. Appreciate you noticing. It'll pass."
"Nice. Sit. The fire's warm."
"I can breathe all the way down again. I couldn't, before you sat down."
"Still on that hard time."
"Alright. But I'm not carrying your stuff."
"Right. Action time. You know where to find me."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"Thanks for... you know. Just listening."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
«Cześć! Ty... jak się nazywasz?» → "Hi! You... what's your name?"

«Tak, tak, dokładnie.» → "Yes, yes, exactly." They nod back, a little quicker this time. Something about the way you tilt your head — hearing them twice, once in their voice and once in the System’s. It unsettles them, a little.
«Dzięki, że jesteś.» → "Thanks for being here." A smile, tired but real.
«Jesteś dobrym człowiekiem.» → "You're a good person." You point at yourself, then at them, then at the fire. Together. They get it. "Food?" — they grin, proud of the one English they know.
You listen hard, watching their mouth shape the words. «To ty... jesteś tu szefem?» → "Is it you... you're the boss here?"
A final shared look — you both feel the talk running its course.
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"This was good." They mean it.
"Can I tell you something? I'm practicing what I would say if I ever saw my family again. I haven't told anyone."
"Thank you. I needed someone to know, and now someone does. Please keep it there."
"You're really going to make me say it again?" Maya rubs their face. "Fine — but it's the same truth as last time."
"We went over this," Maya says, a little tired. "I already told you the truth about that."
"The cistern's nearly dry — 9 liters left. I need someone to haul water with me at first light. Two of us, half the trips. Will you come?"
"Do the math with me: 9 liters, 7 people. That's not tomorrow's water. We walk together and each carry two liters back. Creek water still needs boiling."
Your partner is inside the Haven hall. Go through the door to meet them.
"Okay — I need to move. But I'm glad we talked."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"...Think about it? I'll be around."
"This was good." They mean it.
"We never finished talking about what's been happening — we left it mid-thought, 4 days back. 'And... scene. Good talk.'"
"I keep turning over the last thing Carolina said to me. I can't tell if I'm remembering it right, and that's somehow the worst part."
"We bury, we grieve, we keep going. There's no step four."
"Still on what's been happening."
"I don't do parties. ...It's not you. It's the party."
"Right — go on, I'm listening."
"We're down to 9 liters of clean water. Haul the creek with me at dawn? Two buckets each, there and back."
"9 liters. That's today's drinking water, and then we're boiling creek water and hoping. We walk together and each carry two liters back. Creek water still needs boiling."
Move next to your partner, on the same side of the Haven door.
"Okay. We'll pick this up later."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"...Think about it? I'll be around."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"I'm sorry — I can't shake it. I'm achy and wrung out, barely keeping food down. Can you do anything?"
"The fever's not breaking and I'm barely keeping food down. I need help — real help, not just water."
You spend time tending them. This was care, not a promise of a cure.
"Still on that sickness help."
"Forget I said anything. What did you want?"
"Good question." "The Vigil. They just... took you. Came back like nothing happened. It wasn't nothing."
"Same weather, different day. I keep notes."
"A name. Okay." You say it out loud, trying the shape of it:
🤝 "The Company." It hangs in the air a moment — then Maya grins. It's real now. It has a name, which means it can be lost.
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
🤝 Maya is 👁️ Scout now. Sees trouble first. Warns the party on the road.
"Same as always: we endure."
"I've got fires to light — metaphorical ones. Mostly."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"This was good." They mean it.
Groups make decisions slow and loud. I'll help. From over there.
Naran has an edge today — something curdled.
"I think better when it's quiet. And out here, thinking is surviving."
"I'll show up when it matters. The rest of the time, I'm elsewhere. That's the deal."
"Still on wanting to be left alone."
"...Fine. This had better be worth it."
"Anyway — that's my cross to carry. What's on your mind?"
"You asked me that before. It's a different question now." "They took you — The Vigil, on the screens. The whole fire watched. Nobody knew where to look."
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
Maya nods, stepping back. "Scout is yours now." (Roles are promises. There's only one of each.)
You show them Wild Onion — where it grows, how to tell it apart. "Huh." They turn it over in their mind. "I'll remember that one."
"Alright — I should get back to it."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"...Think about it? I'll be around."
"Good — what's been happening, settled. Feels better said out loud."
"This was good." They mean it.

lines: d42: 📖 The Codex turns a page on its own. Carolina Morales is dead. You didn't ask. It knew.
d42: Nobody's talking much. The fire feels smaller tonight.
d42: 🕯️ Carolina Morales is dead — the expedition. The village stops. Somebody screams. Somebody else starts digging.
d42: What Carolina kept close goes into the ground with them — keepsakes are buried, never taken from the body.
d42: "Carolina's gone." Naran looks at you for a long moment. "You're not Carolina." No heat in it. Just fact. You'll have to earn this face.
d42: The Codex doesn't pause for grief. Elijah blinks — and it's already there, overlaying everything, syncing. No pen. No paper. The mantle just... transfers.
d42: 🌟 "MANTLE TRANSFER DETECTED. ...Oh! New face! Same job! Whole new set of tricks. We hardly noticed. (That is a lie. We noticed. The audience CRIED.)"
d42: 📖 The Codex turns a page: Carolina Morales, 42 days. The mantle passes to Elijah Scott.
d42: 🪞 You wake up somebody else. Elijah Scott, 58 — a Social worker. His hands know different work now: Green Whisper, Translator.
d42: The village's quarrel was with Carolina — and Carolina is dead. The sentence doesn't cross the grave. You're someone else now; the docket is empty, but the village remembers.
d42: At the grave, Naran, Marcus speak for Elijah — "Carolina trusted them. We saw it. Give them the fire's hearing." The village listens.
d42: The fire knew Elijah before the Codex did — his name already carried weight here.

lastSay: d59: Somkiat is showing Pelagia how to tie a snare. Hands patient. It takes three tries.
d59: Mateo drew Wild Ginger in the dirt for the others. It'll wash away. The knowledge won't.
d59: Mateo: "Wild Ginger is coming back thick on the damp slope. Not new — but it's holding."
d59: ⚠ Haven's pantry is empty. Day 5 of hunger.
d59: Haven couldn't hold. On the fifth hungry day, people started walking — in different directions. The scattering, again.
